global_signals.name: ACLK
global_signals.semantics: Global clock signal. Synchronous signals are sampled on the rising edge.

global_signals.name: ARESETn
global_signals.semantics: Global reset signal, active-LOW. May be asserted asynchronously; deassertion must be synchronous with rising ACLK.

signals.name: AWID
signals.semantics: Identification tag for a write transaction.

signals.name: AWADDR
signals.semantics: Address of the first transfer in a write transaction.

signals.name: AWLEN
signals.semantics: Burst length: exact number of data transfers in the write transaction. Burst_Length = AxLEN+1. AXI3 supports 1-16; AXI4 INCR extends to 1-256.

signals.name: AWSIZE
signals.semantics: Burst size: bytes in each data transfer = 2^AWSIZE.

signals.name: AWBURST
signals.semantics: Burst type: 0b00 FIXED, 0b01 INCR, 0b10 WRAP, 0b11 Reserved.

signals.name: AWLOCK
signals.semantics: Atomic access type. AXI3: 0b00 Normal / 0b01 Exclusive / 0b10 Locked. AXI4: 0 Normal / 1 Exclusive.

signals.name: AWCACHE
signals.semantics: Memory-attribute encoding (Bufferable / Modifiable / Allocate / Other Allocate per Table A4-3).

signals.name: AWPROT
signals.semantics: Protection attributes: [0] Unprivileged/Privileged, [1] Secure/Non-secure, [2] Data/Instruction.

signals.name: AWQOS
signals.semantics: Quality of Service identifier; default 0b0000 means not participating in QoS scheme.

signals.name: AWREGION
signals.semantics: Region indicator — distinguishes up to 16 logical regions within a single slave port.

signals.name: AWUSER
signals.semantics: User-defined extension for the write address channel.

signals.name: AWVALID
signals.semantics: Indicates write address channel signals are valid. Must remain HIGH until handshake.

signals.name: AWREADY
signals.semantics: Indicates a transfer on the write address channel can be accepted.

signals.name: WID
signals.semantics: ID tag of the write data transfer. Implemented in AXI3 ONLY (removed in AXI4).

signals.name: WDATA
signals.semantics: Write data payload.

signals.name: WSTRB
signals.semantics: Write strobes — one per byte lane; WSTRB[n] corresponds to WDATA[(8n+7):8n].

signals.name: WLAST
signals.semantics: Indicates this is the last data transfer in the write transaction.

signals.name: WUSER
signals.semantics: User-defined extension for the write data channel.

signals.name: WVALID
signals.semantics: Indicates W channel signals are valid. Must remain HIGH until WREADY handshake.

signals.name: WREADY
signals.semantics: Indicates that a transfer on the write data channel can be accepted.

signals.name: BID
signals.semantics: Identification tag for the write response — must match the AWID of the transaction being responded to.

signals.name: BRESP
signals.semantics: Write response status: 0b00 OKAY, 0b01 EXOKAY, 0b10 SLVERR, 0b11 DECERR.

signals.name: BUSER
signals.semantics: User-defined extension for the write response channel.

signals.name: BVALID
signals.semantics: Indicates a valid write response. Must remain HIGH until handshake.

signals.name: BREADY
signals.semantics: Indicates that a transfer on the write response channel can be accepted.

signals.name: ARID
signals.semantics: Identification tag for a read transaction.

signals.name: ARADDR
signals.semantics: Address of the first transfer in a read transaction.

signals.name: ARLEN
signals.semantics: Burst length: exact number of read data transfers. Burst_Length = ARLEN+1.

signals.name: ARSIZE
signals.semantics: Burst size: bytes per beat = 2^ARSIZE.

signals.name: ARBURST
signals.semantics: Burst type: FIXED/INCR/WRAP/Reserved.

signals.name: ARLOCK
signals.semantics: Atomic access type. AXI3: Normal/Exclusive/Locked. AXI4: Normal/Exclusive.

signals.name: ARCACHE
signals.semantics: Memory-attribute encoding for reads (Bufferable / Modifiable / Allocate / Other Allocate, Table A4-4).

signals.name: ARPROT
signals.semantics: Protection attributes: privilege / security / data-vs-instruction.

signals.name: ARQOS
signals.semantics: Quality of Service identifier.

signals.name: ARREGION
signals.semantics: Region indicator.

signals.name: ARUSER
signals.semantics: User-defined extension for the read address channel.

signals.name: ARVALID
signals.semantics: Indicates AR channel signals are valid.

signals.name: ARREADY
signals.semantics: Indicates that a transfer on the read address channel can be accepted.

signals.name: RID
signals.semantics: Identification tag for read data and response — must match ARID of the corresponding transaction.

signals.name: RDATA
signals.semantics: Read data payload.

signals.name: RRESP
signals.semantics: Read response status: OKAY/EXOKAY/SLVERR/DECERR (slave may signal different responses per beat).

signals.name: RLAST
signals.semantics: Indicates this is the last data transfer in the read transaction.

signals.name: RUSER
signals.semantics: User-defined extension for the read data channel.

signals.name: RVALID
signals.semantics: Indicates R channel signals are valid. Slave can only assert in response to a request for data.

signals.name: RREADY
signals.semantics: Indicates that a transfer on the read data channel can be accepted.

dependency_graph.common_rule: VALID must not depend (combinationally) on READY. A source may not wait for READY before asserting VALID. A receiver may assert READY before or after VALID.
dependency_graph.AXI_read: ARVALID asserted independently of ARREADY. Slave must wait for both ARVALID and ARREADY before asserting RVALID. RVALID independent of RREADY.
dependency_graph.AXI3_write: AWVALID and WVALID asserted independently of AWREADY/WREADY. Slave must wait for WVALID, WREADY, and WLAST before asserting BVALID. BVALID may be asserted BEFORE AW handshake completes (AXI3 only).
dependency_graph.AXI4_write: AWVALID and WVALID asserted independently of AWREADY/WREADY. Slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, WREADY, AND WLAST before asserting BVALID. AXI4 adds the AW handshake as a precondition for BVALID.

ordering_rules.read_data_ordering: Interconnect must ensure that read data from a sequence of transactions with the same ARID targeting different slaves is delivered to the master in the order the addresses were issued. Read data reordering depth is the static count of pending addresses in a slave that may be reordered.
ordering_rules.write_data_ordering: Master must issue write data in the same order as transaction addresses. AXI4+ removes WID and prohibits write data interleaving.
ordering_rules.response_ordering: Transaction responses with the same ID are returned in the same order as the requests were issued. No ordering between different IDs, different masters, or read-vs-write.
ordering_rules.same_id_same_destination: Transaction requests on the same channel, with the same ID and destination are guaranteed to remain in order.

evidence.quote: ACLK Clock source — Global clock signal. ARESETn Reset source — Global reset signal, active-LOW.

AWID, AWADDR, AWLEN (changes between AXI3 and AXI4), AWSIZE, AWBURST, AWLOCK (changes between AXI3 and AXI4), AWCACHE, AWPROT, AWQOS (Not implemented in AXI3), AWREGION (Not implemented in AXI3), AWUSER (Not implemented in AXI3), AWVALID, AWREADY.
WID — The ID tag of the write data transfer. Implemented in AXI3 only. WDATA, WSTRB, WLAST, WUSER (Not implemented in AXI3), WVALID, WREADY.
BID, BRESP, BUSER (Not implemented in AXI3), BVALID, BREADY.

ARID, ARADDR, ARLEN (changes between AXI3 and AXI4), ARSIZE, ARBURST, ARLOCK (changes between AXI3 and AXI4), ARCACHE, ARPROT, ARQOS (Not implemented in AXI3), ARREGION (Not implemented in AXI3), ARUSER (Not implemented in AXI3), ARVALID, ARREADY.
RID, RDATA, RRESP, RLAST, RUSER (Not implemented in AXI3), RVALID, RREADY.
Each channel has its own VALID/READY handshake signal pair (Table A3-1).
AXI3 BVALID requires WVALID/WREADY/WLAST. AXI4 BVALID requires AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, WREADY (and WLAST).

evidence.spec_section: A5.2 ID signals / Table A5-1 / read+write data ordering
evidence.quote: RID must match ARID; master must issue write data in same order as addresses; AXI4 deprecates write-data interleaving.

Transaction requests on the same channel, with the same ID and destination are guaranteed to remain in order. Transaction responses with the same ID are returned in the same order as the requests were issued.
